Hello, Nest
Every new bird in the nest gets a greeting. Read a name and greet it.
A single line with a name: 1 to 30 English letters.
Print `Hello, NAME!` where NAME is the given name.
Two Numbers
Read two integers and print their sum. Python integers never overflow, so the numbers can be huge.
One line with two integers a and b (−10^18 ≤ a, b ≤ 10^18), separated by a space.
Print a + b.
Even or Odd
Decide whether a number is even or odd.
One integer n (−10^9 ≤ n ≤ 10^9).
Print `EVEN` if n is even, otherwise print `ODD`.
Tallest of Three
Three friends measured their heights. Who is the tallest? Print the largest of three numbers.
One line with three integers (1 ≤ each ≤ 300).
Print the largest of the three.
Vowel Counter
Count how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u — upper or lower case) appear in a line of text.
One line of text, 1 to 1000 characters long. It may contain spaces and punctuation.
Print the number of vowels.
Backwards Sentence
Print the words of a sentence in reverse order. Words are separated by single spaces.
One line with 1 to 100 words made of letters.
Print the same words in reverse order, separated by single spaces.
Weather Report
Convert a temperature from Celsius to Fahrenheit using F = C × 9 / 5 + 32.
One integer C (−100 ≤ C ≤ 100).
Print F with exactly one digit after the decimal point.
FizzBuzz
For every number from 1 to n print `Fizz` if it is divisible by 3, `Buzz` if it is divisible by 5, `FizzBuzz` if it is divisible by both, and the number itself otherwise.
One integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000).
Print n lines.
Sum and Max
You are given n numbers. Print their sum and their maximum.
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^4). The second line contains n integers (−10^9 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^9).
Print the sum and the maximum separated by a space.
Runner-up
Find the second largest distinct value in a list. If all values are equal there is no runner-up: print -1.
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^4). The second line contains n integers (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^9).
Print the second largest distinct value, or -1.
Mirror Word
A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards. Check each word.
The first line contains t (1 ≤ t ≤ 100). Each of the next t lines contains one word of lowercase letters (length 1 to 100).
For each word print `YES` if it is a palindrome and `NO` otherwise.
Digital Root
Replace a number by the sum of its digits, again and again, until only one digit is left. Print that digit.
One integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 10^18).
Print the final single digit.
Class Report
A teacher has the scores of n students. Print the name of the best student (the first one in the list if there is a tie) and the class average.
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000). Each of the next n lines contains a name (letters only) and a score (0 ≤ score ≤ 100).
Print the best student's name on the first line and the average with exactly two digits after the decimal point on the second line.
Word Popularity
Count how many times each word appears in a text. Print the words from most to least frequent. Words with the same count are printed in alphabetical order.
One line with 1 to 10^4 lowercase words separated by spaces.
For each distinct word print the word and its count on its own line.
Prime Detective
For each number decide whether it is prime. A prime has exactly two divisors: 1 and itself.
The first line contains q (1 ≤ q ≤ 20). Each of the next q lines contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^9).
For each n print `PRIME` or `NOT PRIME`.
Balanced Brackets
A bracket string is balanced if every opening bracket `(`, `[` or `{` is closed by the matching bracket in the right order.
One line with a string of brackets, length 1 to 2·10^4.
Print `YES` if it is balanced, otherwise `NO`.
Range Sums
Answer many questions of the form “what is the sum of elements from position l to position r?”. Positions are numbered from 1.
The first line contains n and q (1 ≤ n, q ≤ 2·10^4). The second line contains n integers (|a_i| ≤ 10^9). Each of the next q lines contains l and r (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ n).
For each question print the sum.
Adding up the range for every question can be too slow. Prefix sums answer each question in one step.
Pair With Target
Is there a pair of different positions i < j such that a_i + a_j equals the target t?
The first line contains n and t (2 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^4, |t| ≤ 2·10^9). The second line contains n integers (|a_i| ≤ 10^9).
Print `YES` or `NO`.
Checking every pair is too slow for n = 2·10^4. Remember the numbers you have already seen in a set.
Squeeze the Letters
Run-length encoding writes each group of equal letters in a row as the letter followed by the length of the group. For example, `aaabcc` becomes `a3b1c2`.
One line with a string of lowercase letters, length 1 to 2·10^4.
Print the encoded string.
Staircase
Draw a staircase of height n using `#`. Line i (counting from 1) has exactly i `#` characters.
One integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100).
Fewest Coins
You have coins of several values (unlimited of each). What is the smallest number of coins that adds up to exactly S? If it is impossible print -1.
The first line contains k and S (1 ≤ k ≤ 50, 0 ≤ S ≤ 10^4). The second line contains k coin values (1 ≤ c_i ≤ 10^4).
Print the minimum number of coins, or -1.
Greedy (always take the biggest coin) is wrong: with coins 1, 3, 4 and S = 6 the answer is 3 + 3 (2 coins), not 4 + 1 + 1.
Longest Climb
Find the length of the longest run of consecutive elements where each element is strictly greater than the one before it.
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^4). The second line contains n integers.
Print the length of the longest strictly increasing run.
Garden Paths

A garden is an n × m grid. `.` is grass and `#` is a rock. Starting in the top-left cell you can only move right or down. How many different paths reach the bottom-right cell? Print the answer modulo 1 000 000 007.
The first line contains n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 100). The next n lines contain m characters each.
Print the number of paths modulo 10^9 + 7 (0 if the start or the finish is a rock).
How Many Below
You are given n numbers and q questions. For each question x, count how many of the numbers are less than or equal to x.
The first line contains n and q (1 ≤ n, q ≤ 2·10^4). The second line contains n integers. Each of the next q lines contains one integer x. All values are between −10^9 and 10^9.
For each question print the count.
Sort once, then use the bisect module for every question.
Nest Eggs
A bird has n eggs. One nest holds at most k eggs. What is the smallest number of nests needed?
One line with n and k (0 ≤ n ≤ 10^18, 1 ≤ k ≤ 10^18).
Print the number of nests.
Snake Case
Python programmers name variables in snake_case, Java programmers in camelCase. Convert a camelCase name to snake_case: put `_` before every capital letter and make it lowercase.
One word of English letters (length 1 to 100). The first letter is lowercase.
Print the name in snake_case.
Lucky Tickets
A bus ticket has a 6-digit number. It is lucky if the sum of the first three digits equals the sum of the last three.
The first line contains t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000). Each of the next t lines contains a ticket: exactly 6 digits (it may start with zeros).
For each ticket print `LUCKY` or `UNLUCKY`.
Ticket Queue
Simulate a queue. `push x` adds x to the back, `pop` removes the front person, `front` prints the front person. If the queue is empty, `pop` does nothing and `front` prints `EMPTY`.
The first line contains q (1 ≤ q ≤ 2·10^4). Each of the next q lines contains one operation (1 ≤ x ≤ 10^9).
Print the answer to every `front` operation.
Removing from the front of a list is slow. collections.deque has a fast popleft().
Anagram Families
Two words are in the same family if they are anagrams — made of exactly the same letters. How many families are there?
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^4). Each of the next n lines contains a lowercase word (length 1 to 20).
Print the number of families.
Best Streak
A trader writes down the profit (possibly negative) of every day. Find the largest total profit of a block of consecutive days. The block must contain at least one day.
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^4). The second line contains n integers (|a_i| ≤ 10^9).
Print the maximum sum of a non-empty contiguous block.
Try Kadane's algorithm: keep the best sum of a block that ends today.
Clock Hands
Find the smaller angle (in degrees) between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock. The hour hand moves smoothly: at 1:30 it is halfway between 1 and 2.
One line with the time as HH:MM (00 ≤ HH ≤ 23, 00 ≤ MM ≤ 59).
Print the angle with exactly one digit after the decimal point.
Sock Drawer
A drawer has n socks; each has a colour number. Two socks of the same colour make a pair. How many pairs can you make?
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^4). The second line contains n colours (1 ≤ c_i ≤ 100).
Print the number of pairs.
Flip the Table
Transpose a table: rows become columns and columns become rows.
The first line contains n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 100). The next n lines contain m integers each.
Print m lines with n integers each.
Common Divisor
Find the greatest number that divides every element of the list (the GCD of the list).
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^4). The second line contains n integers (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^18).
Print the GCD.
Robot Walk
A robot starts at (0, 0). Each letter moves it one step: `U` y+1, `D` y−1, `L` x−1, `R` x+1. Print its final position and the number of different cells it visited (including the start).
One line with the moves, length 1 to 2·10^4.
Print x, y and the number of visited cells, separated by spaces.
Booking Calendar
A room has n bookings, each from day l to day r inclusive. Merge bookings that overlap or touch (e.g. [1, 3] and [4, 6] touch because day 4 follows day 3) and print the merged bookings in order.
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^4). Each of the next n lines contains l and r (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ 10^9).
Print the number of merged bookings, then each one as `l r` on its own line, sorted by l.
